subject: geography
source_note: Topic structure follows the National Curriculum KS3 programme of study for Geography. Connections, sequence and prerequisites are expert-authored teaching relationships.

units.name: Locational Knowledge
units.blurb: The world's countries, regions and major physical and human features

units.name: Place Knowledge
units.blurb: Comparing a region in Africa and a region in Asia

units.name: Human & Physical Geography
units.blurb: The key physical and human processes that shape the world

units.name: Geographical Skills & Fieldwork
units.blurb: Maps, GIS and collecting and analysing data in the field

topics.name: The World's Countries & Regions
topics.blurb: Africa, Russia, Asia (incl. China and India) and the Middle East

topics.name: Environmental Regions
topics.blurb: Polar and hot deserts, key characteristics, countries and cities

topics.name: Comparing Regions: Africa & Asia
topics.blurb: Human and physical geography of a region in Africa and in Asia

topics.name: Plate Tectonics
topics.blurb: Geological timescales and the movement of plates

topics.name: Rocks, Weathering & Soils
topics.blurb: How rocks form, break down and create soils

topics.name: Weather & Climate
topics.blurb: Weather, climate and change from the Ice Age to the present

topics.name: Glaciation, Hydrology & Coasts
topics.blurb: How ice, water and the sea shape landscapes

topics.name: Population & Urbanisation
topics.blurb: How and where populations grow and concentrate in cities

topics.name: Economic Activity & Sectors
topics.blurb: Primary, secondary, tertiary and quaternary sectors

topics.name: Use of Natural Resources
topics.blurb: How people use the planet's natural resources

topics.name: Human-Physical Interactions
topics.blurb: How human and physical processes change landscapes and climate

topics.name: Globes, Maps & Atlases
topics.blurb: Using globes, maps and atlases routinely

topics.name: Ordnance Survey Maps
topics.blurb: Grid references, scale, thematic mapping and photographs

topics.name: Geographical Information Systems
topics.blurb: Using GIS to view, analyse and interpret data

topics.name: Fieldwork
topics.blurb: Collecting, analysing and concluding from field data

connections.why: Locating the world's countries is the basis for studying their environmental regions
Knowing environmental regions frames the in-depth comparison of African and Asian regions
Place studies of Africa and Asia build on locational knowledge of those continents
Tectonic processes create the rocks that then weather into soils
The resistance of weathered rock shapes how glaciers and coasts erode landscapes
Climate, including past ice ages, drives glaciation and coastal processes
Tectonic and geological processes concentrate many of the resources people use
Urbanisation is closely tied to the shift between economic sectors
Patterns of population growth and urbanisation reflect levels of development
A country's mix of economic sectors is a key measure of its development
Economic activity in every sector depends on extracting and using natural resources
Resource use is a leading way human activity changes landscapes and climate
Human activity now drives changes in the climate system itself
Regional case studies show human and physical processes interacting in real places
Basic atlas skills are the foundation for reading detailed Ordnance Survey maps
Understanding paper maps prepares pupils to analyse spatial data in GIS
OS map skills are used to plan and record observations in the field
GIS is used to analyse and present data collected during fieldwork
Building locational knowledge relies on routine use of globes, maps and atlases
Coastal and glaciated landscapes are common settings for geographical fieldwork
